Checks the paragraph *Coverage in 2015* of the Usage Notes against the composites of
the Alps-wide run (`alps-total/{year}/s1-comp`):

> All years except 2015 contain all 2210 tiles with all twelve layers. In 2015, 89 tiles
> in the north-central Alps contain backscatter but no coherence, and two tiles
> (32TNT14 and 32TNT24) are absent. […] Seven RGI 7.0 glaciers (0.8 km²) lie entirely
> within the tiles without coherence. In 2015, another 46 glaciers have invalid pixels
> in at least one layer, none of them more than 30 %.

The tile counts come from the run manifests. The glacier counts take the RGI 7.0
glaciers (region 11, Central Europe) that intersect the tiles of the scope, rasterized
to the 10 m grid of every tile they intersect, pixel centres inside the outline. A
pixel of a measurement layer (coherence or backscatter, VV or VH) is invalid where it
is NaN, or where the layer, or the whole tile, is missing. The quality layers share
the measurement layer's mask, so they are not read.

A glacier's invalid share of a layer is the share of its pixels that are invalid,
counted over the tiles of one UTM zone, which do not overlap. Along the zone boundaries
a glacier can lie in the tiles of two zones; it then takes the larger of the two
shares, as a user of either tile set sees that much. A glacier counts as without
coherence where both coherence layers are invalid on all of its pixels, and as having
invalid pixels where any layer is invalid on at least one.

```{python}
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
import warnings

from freezebase.mgrs import MGRSGeoBox
from freezebase.raster import rasterio_open
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from rasterio.errors import NotGeoreferencedWarning
from rasterio.features import rasterize

from glace_production.config import settings
from data_paths import run_dirs, run_scope
from glace_production.datasets.rgi import RGI7
from tiles import scope_tiles
```

## Configuration

```{python}
YEAR = 2015
YEARS = range(2015, 2026 + 1)  # for the check that the other years are complete
SCOPE = run_scope()
REPORT_NAME = "coverage-2015"  # CSVs saved in REPORT_DIR
REPORT_DIR = settings.reports_dir / REPORT_NAME  # one folder per notebook
REPORT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
LAYERS = [("COH12", "VV"), ("COH12", "VH"), ("RTC", "VV"), ("RTC", "VH")]
COHERENCE = [f"COH12_{pol}" for pol in ("VV", "VH")]
LAYERS_PER_TILE = 12
WORKERS = 8  # tiles read at once

# The paragraph as it stands in the paper
PAPER = {
    "tiles": 2210,
    "tiles without coherence": 89,
    "absent tiles": "32TNT14, 32TNT24",
    "glaciers without coherence": 7,
    "their area (km²)": 0.8,
    "other glaciers with invalid pixels": 46,
    "all glaciers with invalid pixels": "",
    "largest invalid share (%)": 30,
}
found: dict[str, object] = {}
```

## Tiles

```{python}
def read_manifest(year: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The run manifest of a year: one row per composite file."""
    with (run_dirs(year).comp_dir / "manifest.parquet").open("rb") as f:
        return pd.read_parquet(
            f, columns=["filename", "tile", "product", "polarization", "qa", "stat_valid_percent"]
        )


grid = scope_tiles(SCOPE)
found["tiles"] = len(grid)
print(f"{len(grid)} tiles in the {SCOPE} grid")

completeness = {}
for year in YEARS:
    per_tile = read_manifest(year).groupby("tile").size().reindex(grid["tile"], fill_value=0)
    completeness[year] = {
        "all layers": int((per_tile == LAYERS_PER_TILE).sum()),
        "some layers": int(per_tile.between(1, LAYERS_PER_TILE - 1).sum()),
        "absent": int((per_tile == 0).sum()),
    }
pd.DataFrame(completeness).T
```

```{python}
manifest = read_manifest(YEAR)
assert set(manifest["tile"]) <= set(grid["tile"])
measurements = manifest[manifest["qa"].isna()]
files = measurements.set_index(["tile", "product", "polarization"])["filename"]
products = measurements.groupby("tile")["product"].agg(set)

absent = sorted(set(grid["tile"]) - set(manifest["tile"]))
no_coherence = sorted(products.index[products.map(lambda p: p == {"RTC"})])
found["tiles without coherence"] = len(no_coherence)
found["absent tiles"] = ", ".join(absent)
print(f"{YEAR}: {len(absent)} absent tiles ({', '.join(absent)})")
print(f"{YEAR}: {len(no_coherence)} tiles with backscatter but no coherence")
```

The tiles that can hold invalid pixels: the absent ones, those without coherence, and
those with a measurement layer under 100 % valid in the manifest.

```{python}
partial = measurements.loc[measurements["stat_valid_percent"] < 100, "tile"]
suspect = set(absent) | set(no_coherence) | set(partial)
print(f"{len(set(partial))} tiles with a measurement layer under 100 % valid")
print(f"{len(suspect)} tiles that can hold invalid pixels")
```

## Glaciers

```{python}
rgi = RGI7(product="G", region="11").get_data(download=False)[["area_km2", "geometry"]]
rgi = rgi.to_crs(grid.crs)
in_scope = rgi.iloc[np.unique(grid.sindex.query(rgi.geometry, predicate="intersects")[0])]
suspect_tiles = grid[grid["tile"].isin(suspect)]
candidates = in_scope.iloc[
    np.unique(suspect_tiles.sindex.query(in_scope.geometry, predicate="intersects")[0])
]
# Every tile a candidate intersects, so that its share is taken over all of its pixels
read_tiles = sorted(
    grid["tile"].iloc[np.unique(grid.sindex.query(candidates.geometry, predicate="intersects")[1])]
)
print(f"{len(in_scope)} RGI 7.0 glaciers intersect the scope, {len(candidates)} a suspect tile")
print(f"{len(read_tiles)} tiles to read")
```

Every tile is rasterized with the candidates' positions as labels (RGI outlines do not
overlap), so one `bincount` gives each glacier's pixels and another its invalid ones.

```{python}
projected = {epsg: candidates.to_crs(epsg) for epsg in grid["epsg"].unique()}


def invalid_mask(tile: str, product: str, pol: str, shape: tuple[int, int]) -> np.ndarray:
    """True where a measurement layer of a tile is invalid; all of it if the file is missing."""
    name = files.get((tile, product, pol))
    if name is None:
        return np.ones(shape, dtype=bool)
    with rasterio_open(run_dirs(YEAR).comp_dir / name) as src:
        values = src.read(1)
        nodata = src.nodata
    invalid = ~np.isfinite(values)
    if nodata is not None and not np.isnan(nodata):
        invalid |= values == nodata
    return invalid


def count_tile(tile: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Pixels and invalid pixels per layer of every candidate glacier in one tile."""
    geobox = MGRSGeoBox.from_mgrs(tile)
    shape = (geobox.shape.y, geobox.shape.x)
    glaciers = projected[geobox.crs.epsg]
    inside = glaciers.sindex.query(geobox.extent.geom, predicate="intersects")
    labels = rasterize(
        zip(glaciers.geometry.iloc[inside], inside + 1, strict=True),
        out_shape=shape,
        transform=geobox.transform,
        fill=0,
        dtype="int32",
    )
    n = len(glaciers) + 1
    counts = pd.DataFrame(
        {"position": np.arange(n), "pixels": np.bincount(labels.ravel(), minlength=n)}
    )
    for product, pol in LAYERS:
        invalid = invalid_mask(tile, product, pol, shape)
        counts[f"{product}_{pol}"] = np.bincount(labels[invalid], minlength=n)
    counts = counts[(counts["position"] > 0) & (counts["pixels"] > 0)]
    return counts.assign(tile=tile, epsg=geobox.crs.epsg, position=counts["position"] - 1)


# rasterize warns that its in-memory raster has no transform when it runs in threads,
# though it applies the one it is given: the pixel counts match the RGI areas below.
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=NotGeoreferencedWarning)
with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=WORKERS) as pool:
    counts = pd.concat(pool.map(count_tile, read_tiles), ignore_index=True)
counts["rgi_id"] = candidates.index[counts["position"]]
counts.to_csv(REPORT_DIR / "glacier-tile-pixels.csv", index=False)
```

```{python}
layer_names = [f"{product}_{pol}" for product, pol in LAYERS]
per_zone = counts.groupby(["rgi_id", "epsg"])[["pixels", *layer_names]].sum()
shares = per_zone[layer_names].div(per_zone["pixels"], axis=0).groupby("rgi_id").max()
glaciers = candidates[["area_km2"]].join(shares, how="inner")
glaciers["pixels"] = per_zone["pixels"].groupby("rgi_id").max()
glaciers["max_share"] = glaciers[layer_names].max(axis=1)
glaciers["in_absent_tile"] = glaciers.index.isin(counts.loc[counts["tile"].isin(absent), "rgi_id"])
glaciers["without_coherence"] = (glaciers[COHERENCE] == 1).all(axis=1)
glaciers["within_no_coherence_tiles"] = glaciers.index.isin(
    candidates.index[candidates.within(grid[grid["tile"].isin(no_coherence)].union_all())]
)
glaciers.sort_values("max_share", ascending=False).to_csv(REPORT_DIR / "glaciers.csv")
print(f"{len(candidates) - len(glaciers)} candidates have no pixel centre inside their outline")
print(f"{glaciers['in_absent_tile'].sum()} glaciers have pixels in an absent tile")
```

### Glaciers without coherence

The paper counts the glaciers that lie entirely within the tiles without coherence;
the pixel test, both coherence layers invalid on every pixel, should find the same.

```{python}
without = glaciers[glaciers["without_coherence"]]
within = glaciers[glaciers["within_no_coherence_tiles"]]
found["glaciers without coherence"] = len(without)
found["their area (km²)"] = round(without["area_km2"].sum(), 1)
print(f"no coherence on any pixel: {len(without)} glaciers, {without['area_km2'].sum():.2f} km²")
print(
    f"within the tiles without coherence: {len(within)} glaciers, {within['area_km2'].sum():.2f} km²"
)
print(f"same glaciers: {set(without.index) == set(within.index)}")
without[["area_km2", "pixels", *layer_names]].round(3)
```

### Other glaciers with invalid pixels

```{python}
other = glaciers[~glaciers["without_coherence"] & (glaciers["max_share"] > 0)]
found["other glaciers with invalid pixels"] = len(other)
# with the glaciers without coherence, which also have invalid pixels
found["all glaciers with invalid pixels"] = len(other) + len(without)
found["largest invalid share (%)"] = round(100 * other["max_share"].max(), 1)
by_layer = (other[layer_names] > 0).sum()
print(f"{len(other)} other glaciers with invalid pixels, {other['area_km2'].sum():.1f} km²")
print("glaciers with invalid pixels per layer:", by_layer.to_dict())
print(
    "invalid share, percentiles 50/90/100:",
    np.percentile(100 * other["max_share"], [50, 90, 100]).round(1),
)
other.sort_values("max_share", ascending=False)[
    ["area_km2", "pixels", *layer_names, "max_share"]
].head(15).round(3)
```
